sections.h2: Who keeps property records in Denton County
sections.html:
The County Clerk's Recording Division keeps every real property record for Denton County, along with vital statistics. The office is at 1450 E. McKinney Street, Denton, TX 76209, and it keeps weekday hours from 8 in the morning to half past four.

The county runs six County Clerk locations, and all of them accept passport applications. Real property filings are different. Every recording must go to the Denton location, so a seller in another part of the county cannot drop a deed at a branch office.

  • In person: 1450 E McKinney Street, Denton
  • By mail: Denton County Clerk, Attn: Recording, 1450 E. McKinney St., Denton, TX 76209
  • Electronically: through one of the clerk's listed electronic recording partners

If you file by USPS, FedEx or UPS, include the right request and payment form. The clerk's Recording Division page explains the mail-in route and links the e-recording partners.

Paper filings arrive by mail or at the counter. Electronic filings must go through an approved partner, and you choose a partner before submitting. Each partner can explain its own process.

Mailed packets can be paid with a business check, money order, cashier's check or a credit card, and a card has to be entered on the clerk's Credit Card Payment Form. Over the counter, cash is also accepted. Personal checks are not on the list.

For a copy of something already recorded, the clerk charges $5 for a clerk's certificate, when one is needed, plus $1 for each page or part of a page. A records search done by clerk staff is $10 per entry. A title company usually orders its own copies, so if you only need the deed, ask the title officer before paying for a certificate.

The first page is $25. A required recording information page adds $4, and each page after that is $4. Because the information page is its own line, a deed that looks like one page on paper is still priced for more than one.

Denton County Clerk real property recording fees

The $25 first-page charge includes a $10 Records Management and Preservation Fee and a $10 Records Archive Fee. The county cites Local Government Code Sec. 118.011 for the general fees, Property Code Sec. 14.005 for the federal tax lien and Property Code Sec. 51.002(f) for the notice of sale.

sections.h2: Denton County housing at a glance
sections.html:
Denton County is growing quickly, and its housing is newer and pricier than most of Texas. The July 2025 estimate is 1,069,346 residents, an 18.0 percent rise on the 2020 count of 906,530 and well above the 662,614 counted in 2010. Land area is 878.51 square miles, and density was 1,031.8 residents per square mile in 2020.

  • Housing units: 415,326 in 2025, with 10,210 building permits that year
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 65.5 percent for 2020 to 2024
  • Middle owner-occupied home value: $437,200
  • Median gross rent: $1,728

With that much new building, new construction competes with resale listings all over the county, and many sellers own homes in recorded subdivisions. The plat matters. The clerk files plats at $50 per page, and a copy of a plat on file is $5. A buyer's title company will want the plat and any other recorded restrictions.

sections.h2: What to check in the records before listing
sections.html:
Pull the vesting deed, the deed of trust and any releases, then compare the names and legal description against the tax records. Mismatches are easy to fix before an offer and slow to fix after one.

  • Name and legal description. The seller's name on the deed should match the name on the sale contract, and the lot and block should match the plat.
  • Liens. A state tax lien, federal tax lien or unreleased mortgage will be visible in the clerk's index, and the schedule lists a fee for each filing and for the federal release.
  • Foreclosure posting. The county posts notice of a trustee's sale and charges the clerk's $2 notice fee. Texas sales take place on the first Tuesday of the month.
  • Heirs. For an inherited house, a death-transfer deed has to be on record before the owner dies, and a muniment of title goes to the clerk in the land's home county.

If anything on the list looks off, ask the title officer how the problem gets cleared. Some defects need only a release. Others need a corrective deed or a court order.

sections.h2: How property tax hits a Denton County seller
sections.html:
The tax lien attaches on January 1, so the bill for the year follows the property no matter when the sale closes. Appraisal districts set value as of that date, and tax bills usually go out in October.

The last day to pay without penalty is January 31, and February 1 starts delinquency. The collector then adds a six percent penalty and one percent interest, with the penalty rising to 12 percent on July 1. Homeowners age 65 or older, disabled owners and disabled-veteran owners can pay in four installments.

Texas has no state property tax, so the whole bill comes from local units such as the county, school district and city. Ask the Denton County tax office for the current balance before closing, and ask the appraisal district to confirm any homestead, over-65 or disabled-veteran exemption on file. A school district must give a $140,000 homestead exemption.

Most delays come from paperwork, not price. If the deed has a typo in a name, if a paid-off loan never got a release, or if the owner has died and no one has filed the estate, the closing slips. Start with a list: the vesting deed, each loan, and any lien notice. Hand the list to the title officer on day one.

When a document has to be corrected, the fix is a new recorded instrument. Because every filing must go to the Denton location, build in mailing time or choose an e-recording partner. Allow for the $25 first page plus the required $4 information page when you budget the filing cost.

faqs.q: Which office files a Denton County deed?
faqs.a: The County Clerk's Recording Division, 1450 E. McKinney Street in Denton. You can also mail it to that address or file electronically through a clerk-approved partner. All recordings must go to the Denton location, not to the other clerk offices.

faqs.q: What are the Denton County Clerk's hours?
faqs.a: The Recording Division serves the public on weekdays from 8 in the morning to half past four at 1450 E McKinney Street. Recordings go to that Denton office only.

faqs.q: What does a deed filing cost in Denton County?
faqs.a: $25 for the first page, $4 for a required recording information page and $4 for each additional page, with printing on the back counted as a page. The first-page charge includes $10 for records preservation and $10 for archiving.

faqs.q: What forms of payment does the Denton County recording office accept?
faqs.a: Business checks, cash, cashier's checks, credit cards and money orders. Mail-in filings paid by card need the clerk's Credit Card Payment Form, and mailed filings need the matching request and payment form.

faqs.q: Can I record a document electronically in Denton County?
faqs.a: Yes, but only through one of the clerk's electronic recording partners. Choose a partner first, and it will explain its own steps.
